source: agents' floor plans on Rightmove's sold-price pages for EC1V 8BG (backend/scripts/block/listings.py fetch; images cached, git-ignored), read by eye on 2026-11-09
note: floors as each agent labels them: some count the mezzanine as the first floor (so the penthouses are on 'fourth and fifth'), others use the brochure's names. Areas are the agents' (gross internal, RICS). matches: the brochure unit whose plan this is, by its shape (rooms, stair, chamfer, terraces), turned where noted.

plans.how: ground: reception with the kitchen, WC and stair; upper ('mezzanine', 177 sq ft): bedroom, bath and a void over the reception, as the brochure's M3
bedroom, bath, kitchen/reception round a small hall: the MZ2/F2/F6 type, turned 90 degrees
bedroom with bath; kitchen/living with the kitchen in a wing: the MZ3/F3/F7 type
the chamfered corner, two bedrooms either side of the reception/kitchen, bath and shower by the entrance: the MZ1/F1/F5 type
bedroom and bath beside a kitchen/reception with the kitchen in a wing: the MZ3/F3/F7 type
reception and kitchen across the front, two bedrooms, the entrance corridor down one side: the MZ4/F4/F8 type
the chamfered corner reception, two bedrooms, kitchen and store: the MZ1/F1/F5 type

bath and bedroom above, kitchen and reception below, the door on the left: the MZ2/F2/F6 type drawn as the brochure draws it; labelled First Floor, which is wrong: the user says Flat 14 is on the 2nd floor (2026-11-09), where C-0001 puts F6
bedroom and shower room; reception/kitchen with the kitchen in a wing: the MZ3/F3/F7 type
three bedrooms with an ensuite in the chamfered corner below; reception, dining and kitchen under the chamfer above, a terrace wrapping two sides: F9

the brochure's F10 turned 90 degrees: entrance corridor out of the block, two bedrooms on the front, the stair by the WC; kitchen/reception above with balconies front and back. 1154 sq ft against the brochure's 988
the brochure's F11: the stair in a wing beside the entrance, bathroom and shower room, two bedrooms; kitchen/reception above with the WC in the wing and a balcony along the side
the brochure's F12 turned 180 degrees: the entrance and stair at one end, three bedrooms; reception/dining with terraces both sides above

the penthouse terrace, glass and steel balustrade, looking over the street
